hooks.text: Think the Moon doesn't spin? That is a total myth.
Did you know the Moon actually rotates on its axis?
The Moon spins on its axis every single lunar orbit.

title: Why We Only Ever See One Side of the Moon
description: Discover the truth about tidal locking and how the Soviet Luna 3 spacecraft first photographed the hidden far side of the Moon in 1959.

beats.text: Think the Moon doesn't spin? That is a total myth.
beats.visual: Earth and Moon from space, Apollo 8 photograph, 1968
queries: Earth and Moon from space Apollo 8

beats.text: The Moon actually rotates on its axis at the exact same speed it orbits our home planet.
beats.visual: Tidal locking diagram illustrating synchronous rotation

beats.text: This cosmic synchronization keeps the exact same side facing Earth forever.
beats.visual: Diagram of gravitational tidal bulges on the Moon

beats.text: Earth's immense gravity constantly stretches the Moon into tidal bulges that generate gravitational torque.
beats.visual: Illustration of gravitational forces between Earth and Moon

beats.text: In 1959, the Soviet spacecraft Luna 3 successfully transmitted the very first photographs of the far side.
beats.visual: Luna 3 spacecraft model and far side photographs, 1959
queries: Luna 3 far side of the Moon

beats.text: This tidal locking is precisely why humanity never caught a single glimpse of that hidden hemisphere before.
beats.visual: First photograph of the far side of the Moon by Luna 3, 1959

beats.text: Because tidal locking ensures the Moon's rotation matches its orbit, you have to wonder if it ever stays still.
beats.visual: Earth and Moon from space, Apollo 17 photograph, 1972
